verdict.rationale: E2B's SDK documents every step of the loop programmatically. The agent can create a sandbox (Sandbox.create), run code (runCode, commands.run), read results and files (files.read, files.list), and tear down with `kill`. Non-interactive API-key auth and LLM tool-use integration let an agent drive this with no human involved. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration that an agent runs the full provision-to-teardown lifecycle autonomously.

support.subject: As an ai-native user, my agent can provision its own sandbox, execute code, read the results, and tear it down — end to end without a human

citations.quote:
const sbx = await Sandbox.create() // Creates a persistent sandbox session
const execution = await sbx.runCode('print("hello world")')
You can read files from the sandbox filesystem using the `files.read()` method.
You can shutdown the sandbox any time even before the timeout is up by calling the `kill` method.
E2B can work with any LLM and AI framework. The easiest way to connect an LLM to E2B is to use the tool use capabilities of the LLM
This is the recommended option for non-interactive environments like CI/CD pipelines, servers, and containers.
